findings.title: remove() always hits DB to fetch storedIdp even when cache is valid
findings.body: The modified `remove(alias)` method now unconditionally calls `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` at the top of the method to obtain `storedIdp` for `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. The previous code only invoked `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` when `isInvalid(cacheKey)` was true (the common-case fast path used the cached `CachedIdentityProvider`). After this change, every `remove` performs a DB lookup even when the alias is fully cached, turning what was an O(1) cache hit into an extra JPA roundtrip on the hot path for IDP removal.

findings.title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation invalidates all FetchMode caches unnecessarily
findings.body: `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` registers invalidation for every `FetchMode` (REALM_ONLY, ORG_ONLY, ALL) whenever the affected IDP passes the login predicate. However, a realm-only login IDP can only appear in the REALM_ONLY and ALL caches, and an org-bound login IDP can only appear in the ORG_ONLY and ALL caches. Invalidating the third cache (e.g. wiping ORG_ONLY results when creating a realm-only IDP) discards valid cached entries that have no relationship to the change, forcing the next call in that mode to repopulate from the DB unnecessarily. The predicate already exposes whether the IDP has an organizationId, so a targeted invalidation per affected mode would be straightforward.

findings.title: New isEnabled() re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean has no test
findings.body: The PR adds `idp.isEnabled() && ...` filters to both the `ORG_ONLY` and `ALL` branches of `searchForIdentityProviders`, with a comment explaining that the re-check is needed because the cached IDP model is wrapped and `isEnabled()` may return false when the bound organization is disabled. There is no test in `OrganizationCacheTest` (or elsewhere in the diff) that exercises this re-check path - e.g. a test that disables the organization bound to a cached IDP and verifies the login page no longer shows the IDP. Without such a test, a future refactor that removes the re-check (thinking the cached wrapper already handles it) would silently regress this behavior.
